title: DR1 asks the user to search for a commodity by common name, code or Latin name; the frontend prints the whole catalogue as a static checkbox list with no search control at all.

finding.frontend: Under the heading "What are you importing?" the user meets the entire commodity catalogue at once: five checkbox fieldsets, legended Cow (0102), Horse (0101), Cat (01061900), Dog (01061900) and Fish (0301), holding eight species between them, every one of them rendered on arrival. There is no text box, no search button, no filter and no result count. The template loops over every group the commodity service returns and prints it, in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:20-29. The corpus names this screen fe-commodity-search and the page does not search.
finding.prototype: The same page opens on an empty labelled search box — the label is "Search for a commodity", the hint is "You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus)", and a magnifying-glass button sits inside the field (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:48-116). Nothing else is on the page until the user types. A search returns a grouped result list rendered beneath the input: a commodity header row carrying the name and code with the matched text emphasised, then one checkbox per matching species under it, and the number of matches is announced through a polite live region — the captured results state shows a "cattle" search returning a Cattle (0102) header and eleven species, with "11 results available" in the status region.
finding.difference: Replace the static grouped checkbox list with a search control: a labelled input named commoditySearch carrying DR1's hint, a search button, results grouped under a commodity header row with the matched substring emphasised, and a polite live region announcing the number of matches. The list must become the result of searching rather than the whole catalogue printed on arrival — the search sits in place of the current fieldsets, not above them. Nothing blocks this, but it is the natural home for two findings that travel with it: the wider catalogue the search would be searching (commodities--commodity-catalogue) and the running selection summary a transient result list needs (commodities--search-selection-summary).
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any text input, search box or filter control on the frontend's commodity page in any state. Its rendered DOM holds no input element other than the CSRF token and the eight species checkboxes, and the list is not paged or filtered, so no other state can introduce one.
